evals.prompt: Review my branch feature/bulk-invite since main. The commits reference #412 which is the issue for bulk-inviting users from a CSV.
evals.expected_output: Plans a two-axis review (Standards and Spec) of git diff main...HEAD, run as two parallel sub-agents, reported side by side without reranking.
expectations: Uses a three-dot diff against the fixed point (git diff main...HEAD) and lists commits with git log main..HEAD
Validates the fixed point resolves and the diff is non-empty before spawning sub-agents
Fetches issue #412 as the spec source for the Spec axis
Spawns Standards and Spec reviews as two parallel sub-agents
Presents results under separate '## Standards' and '## Spec' headings without merging or reranking across axes

evals.prompt: Can you do a code review of the last 5 commits on this branch? There's no ticket for it, it was a quick refactor of the pricing module.
evals.expected_output: Reviews HEAD~5...HEAD on the Standards axis including the Fowler smell baseline, skips the Spec sub-agent and notes no spec is available.
expectations: Uses HEAD~5 as the fixed point
Skips the Spec sub-agent and reports 'no spec available' (or equivalent) since the user said there is no ticket
Includes the Fowler code-smell baseline (e.g. Feature Envy, Data Clumps, Primitive Obsession, Shotgun Surgery) in the Standards review
Treats baseline smells as judgement calls (e.g. 'possible Feature Envy') rather than hard violations
Looks for repo-documented standards (e.g. CONTRIBUTING.md, CODING_STANDARDS.md) and notes they override the smell baseline

evals.expected_output: Asks the user for the fixed point (commit, branch, tag) to diff against rather than guessing.
expectations: Asks the user which fixed point (commit SHA, branch, tag, or merge-base) to review since, rather than assuming one
Describes that the review will cover two axes: Standards and Spec
Mentions looking for the originating spec via issue references in commit messages, a passed path, or docs/specs/.scratch files
